speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. Can you describe when this rash and numbness on your palms first started, and have you noticed any specific triggers that make it worse?

speaker: Patient
text: 50-year-old male. The patient reports a year-long history of an itchy rash on his upper body and face. Additionally, he has been experiencing a numbness and tingling sensation on both palms. He has been working on his family's rice farm, also caring for livestock.

speaker: Doctor
text: I see, given your work with livestock and rice farming, has the rash appeared only on areas exposed to sunlight, or is it also present on covered parts of your body?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Pruritic rash on upper body and face. I also have Numbness and tingling sensation of both palms, Thinning of the eyebrows, Loss of some eyelashes, Hypopigmented macules around the elbows.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the combination of your hypopigmented macules, eyebrow and eyelash loss, and the numbness in your palms, I need to check your reflexes and sensation more closely. Do you have a family history of similar skin or nerve issues, and have you noticed any muscle weakness? REQUEST IMAGES: Dermatology_Skin_Biopsy

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: No significant past medical history. Social history: Works as a farmer, no history of travel outside the local area.

speaker: Doctor
text: The combination of hypopigmented macules, madarosis (eyebrow and eyelash loss), and sensory loss on your palms is highly suspicious for leprosy. To confirm this, I need to verify if your palms are thickened and to check for specific nerve involvement. Do you feel any loss of sensation to a pinprick on your fingertips, and are your earlobes thickened? REQUEST TEST: Slit_Skin_Smear

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Skin Biopsy: Chronic inflammatory cells with features suggestive of leprosy. Nerve Conduction Studies: Reduced sensory nerve action potentials in the ulnar nerves. Serology: Anti-PGL-1 antibodies Positive.

speaker: Doctor
text: The biopsy, nerve studies, and positive serology confirm a diagnosis of leprosy, specifically the borderline or lepromatous type given your skin and nerve findings. DIAGNOSIS READY: Lepromatous Leprosy
